statement: Targeted behaviors in transformer language models are causally mediated by small, localizable component sets — single directions, sparse neuron sets, mid-layer MLP computations — and weight-space interventions at those sites produce large changes in the targeted behavior.
perturbation_kind: mixed: neuron ablation/amplification, direction ablation, rank-one FFN edit
observed_effect: Vig et al.: gender-bias effects are 'concentrated in specific components' and manifest in 'a relatively small proportion of neurons and attention heads'. ROME: a causal intervention reveals 'a distinct set of steps in middle-layer feed-forward modules that mediate factual predictions while processing subject tokens'; rank-one edits there update the target fact while the method 'simultaneously maintains both specificity and generalization, whereas other methods sacrifice one or another'. Dai et al.: identified knowledge-neuron activation is 'positively correlated to the expression of their corresponding facts'. Arditi et al.: refusal 'is mediated by a one-dimensional subspace' across 13 chat models up to 72B. Liu et al.: about 50 FFN neurons (0.014% of all neurons) control the refusal template.
scope: Transformer LMs: BERT cloze, GPT-2 XL, GPT-J/NeoX-class, 13 open chat models up to 72B, 13 models across 4 architecture families; behaviors with dedicated circuits (factual recall, gender-bias completion, refusal, refusal template, sycophancy). Not established for behaviors without a single causal component.
confidence_note: Five papers, four independent groups, 2020-2026, behaviors from factual recall to refusal. Localization evidence comes from activation-space perturbation (patching/mediation) while the durable edits are weight-space; both spaces agree on sparsity. Boundary: routing-type circuits resist single-direction steering in most models (see O04); the anchor case's Gemma control ('no single component to switch off') is consistent with that boundary but is documented in the skill itself, not resolved as literature here.

statement: A fine-tuned-minus-pretrained weight delta (a task vector) acts as a direction in weight space: adding it steers the model toward the fine-tuned behavior, negating it removes that behavior with little change on control tasks, and multiple task vectors compose — with the caveat that naive composition loses information through parameter interference.
observed_effect: Ilharco et al.: 'Negating a task vector decreases performance on the target task, with little change in model behavior on control tasks'; 'adding task vectors together can improve performance on multiple tasks at once'; analogy-composition (A is to B as C is to D) improves the fourth task with no training data from it. Yadav et al.: existing merging ignores 'the interference between parameters of different models, resulting in large performance drops'; two sources — 'interference due to redundant parameter values and (b) disagreement on the sign of a given parameter's values'; TIES (trim, elect sign, merge) outperforms prior merging across modalities, domains, model sizes and architectures.
scope: Pre-trained models across modalities and families (CLIP/ViT, NLP fine-tunes including T0-class), several tasks and sizes; weight-space arithmetic is confined to a single base model.
confidence_note: Two independent groups. TIES bounds the principle: superposition of task vectors is lossy without sign/magnitude resolution — treat merges as edits needing their own verification, not free composition.

statement: A knowledge edit that succeeds on its direct probe does not reliably integrate with the model's surrounding knowledge: entailed multi-hop answers fail to update, and implications for related facts (ripple effects) are neither consistently propagated nor consistently preserved — so an edit's verification must extend well beyond the edited fact.
perturbation_kind: rank-one / memory edits evaluated for propagation (ROME-, MEMIT-, MEND-, KN-class editors)
observed_effect: Cohen et al.: 'injecting one fact ... introduces a ripple effect in the form of additional facts that the model needs to update'; on the RippleEdits benchmark (5K factual edits, six criteria) 'current methods fail to introduce consistent changes in the model's knowledge'. Zhong et al.: on MQuAKE, edited models fail multi-hop questions whose answers 'should change as an entailed consequence of edited facts'; the non-parametric MeLLo baseline outperforms parametric editors by a large margin. Yao et al.: 'enduring issues intrinsic to existing techniques' across method families.
scope: GPT-J, GPT-NeoX, LLaMA/Vicuna-class editors; single-fact and batch factual edits. The failure runs both ways: needed propagation does not happen, and things that should stay fixed do not.
confidence_note: Three independent groups, two evaluation paradigms (ripple criteria; multi-hop). A memory-based in-context baseline beating the weight-space editors shows the deficit is specific to the weight-space methods tested, not to the benchmarks.

statement: Broad behavioral modes can be steered by low-rank — often single-direction — interventions in activation space: adding or ablating one residual-stream direction elicits or removes refusal across many chat models, and adding prompt-contrast steering vectors shifts sentiment and toxicity model-wide, with both papers reporting general capabilities preserved.
observed_effect: Arditi et al.: 'erasing this direction from the model's residual stream activations prevents it from refusing harmful instructions, while adding this direction elicits refusal on even harmless instructions'; the intervention 'surgically disables refusal with minimal effect on other capabilities' (13 open chat models up to 72B). Turner et al.: activation engineering 'strategically perturbs activations at inference time'; ActAdd 'achieves SOTA on toxicity reduction and sentiment control', and the steered models are 'thoroughly test[ed] ... to verify the preservation of their general capabilities'.
scope: GPT-2-family and LLaMA-2 7B/13B (Turner) and 13 open chat models up to 72B (Arditi); inference-time residual-stream interventions on model-level modes (refusal, sentiment, toxicity). Contrast O04: the same low-rank assumption fails for routing-type circuits in 16 of 19 models.
confidence_note: Two independent groups, different behaviors (safety refusal; sentiment/toxicity). Preservation is as-reported by the authors' own capability checks, not independently audited here.

statement: Establishing which internals carry a behavior requires interventional observation — perturbing components and measuring the effect — not observational probing: probing-style methods can show information exists, while causal mediation analysis, causal tracing / activation patching, and perturbation probing show it is used.
perturbation_kind: methodology: activation patch / causal mediation / two-pass perturbation probe
observed_effect: Vig et al.: methods that read hidden representations 'can only measure whether the information exists, not whether it is actually used by the model'; their causal mediation analysis identifies which parts are 'causally implicated in its behavior'. Zhang & Nanda: 'Activation patching, also known as causal tracing or interchange intervention, is a standard technique for this task (Vig et al., 2020), but the literature contains many variants with little consensus on the choice of hyperparameters or methodology'. Liu et al.: perturbation probing 'generates task-specific causal hypotheses for FFN neurons in large language models using two forward passes per prompt and no backpropagation, followed by a one-time intervention sweep' that validates causality.
scope: Transformer LMs broadly; the methodological backbone of locate-then-edit and of this skill's Localize and intervene gates. Methodological entry — propagation not applicable.
confidence_note: Methodological entry: propagation n/a. Three papers spanning 2020-2026 naming one practice under evolving names (causal mediation -> causal tracing / activation patching -> perturbation probing). See O06 for the methodology-sensitivity caveat before trusting any single localization.

statement: High-level concepts are represented linearly as directions in the model's representation space — the linear representation hypothesis — which is what makes a single direction the domain's unit of intervention: formalized through counterfactuals with provable connections to probing and steering, and demonstrated behaviorally by single-direction mediation of refusal across many chat models.
perturbation_kind: methodology/theory: linear representation; direction add / ablate
observed_effect: Park et al.: 'high-level concepts are represented linearly as directions in some representation space' — the linear representation hypothesis, formalized through counterfactuals, with provable connections to probing (output space) and steering (input space). Arditi et al.: 'erasing this direction from the model's residual stream activations prevents it from refusing harmful instructions, while adding this direction elicits refusal on even harmless instructions' — refusal is 'mediated by a one-dimensional subspace' across 13 open chat models up to 72B.
scope: Transformer LMs; one theory formalization (Park/Choe/Veitch, ICML 2024) plus one behavioral demonstration on safety refusal across 13 open chat models up to 72B (Arditi et al., NeurIPS 2024). Theory/methodology entry — propagation not applicable. Grounds why direction-based interventions (steering, ablation, rank-one write-downs of a direction) are constructible at all; see P04/O04 for where single-direction interventions stop generalizing.
confidence_note: Two independent groups (theory; empirical). Boundary carried from Sharkey et al.'s catalog (full text, run ac3ac4bc3af5f4db): the strong version (all concepts linear) is false for some models (Black et al., 2022; Csordas et al., 2024) — the principle carries the weak version.

statement: Activation-space intervention directions can be transferred across independently trained language models through learned or affine mappings of shared representation spaces — but the transfer is conditional, with measured representational-capacity and stability requirements; it does not extend to raw weight deltas, which remain confined to a single base model (P02 scope).
perturbation_kind: direction transfer across models (learned mappings / affine stitching / universal vectors)
observed_effect: Agarwal: 'shared LLM geometry is functionally exploitable, conditionally' — 47-49% of cross-model feature pairs validate at >=1.7B (Pearson r >= 0.60; Procrustes cosines 0.895-0.956); 'alignment degrades sharply below 0.8B'; a single universal vector achieved 67.3% in 4 of 5 models; transfer fails under generation instability. Oozeer et al.: 'safety interventions can be transferred between models through learned mappings of their shared activation spaces' — backdoor removal and refusal steering transfer across Llama/Qwen/Gemma; smaller models can align larger ones. Chen et al.: 'affine mappings between residual streams' are a 'cheap way to effectively transfer represented features between models' — SAEs, probes and steering vectors transfer across model sizes; semantic and structural features transfer differently.
scope: Open chat models across Llama/Qwen/Gemma families, 0.8B-72B; activation/representation-space directions only — weight-space deltas are base-confined (P02). Conditions measured: scale (validated zone >=1.7B; sharp degradation below 0.8B), family (transfer crosses families via learned mappings), generation stability. Transfer/methodology entry — propagation not applicable.
confidence_note: Three independent groups (2025-2026), three transfer mechanisms (universal steering vectors; learned safety-intervention mappings; affine residual-stream stitching), one conditional-transfer conclusion. Each specific condition is single-paper: the ~1.7B discontinuity is Agarwal's own measurement; the semantic-vs-structural distinction is Chen et al.'s own. The direct-model-edit anchor model (0.8B) sits below the validated zone — the least-supported region of the map.

statement: Batch weight editing at shared mid-layer MLP sites scales to thousands of stored associations in one model — orders of magnitude beyond single-edit methods — with edit-quality metrics declining as the number of simultaneous edits grows.
observed_effect: 'MEMIT, a method for directly updating a language model with many memories, demonstrating experimentally that it can scale up to thousands of associations for GPT-J (6B) and GPT-NeoX (20B), exceeding prior work by orders of magnitude'; the paper's counterfactual scaling curves decline from roughly 80% at single-digit edit counts toward ~50% at hundreds of simultaneous edits.
scope: GPT-J (6B) and GPT-NeoX (20B); factual associations stored at the critical mid-layer MLP sites identified via causal mediation.
confidence_note: Single paper (ICLR 2023), same group as ROME — not independent for the localization claim. Decline figures read from the paper's scaling table as surfaced in server-recorded search content.

statement: Individual FFN neurons identified by integrated-gradients attribution carry specific facts: their activation tracks fact expression, and suppressing or amplifying them — or editing their output weights — updates or erases the fact without fine-tuning.
perturbation_kind: neuron suppress / amplify; FFN output-row edit
observed_effect: 'We find that the activation of such knowledge neurons is positively correlated to the expression of their corresponding facts'; case studies 'attempt to leverage knowledge neurons to edit (such as update, and erase) specific factual knowledge without fine-tuning'.
scope: BERT masked-LM cloze tasks; the authors frame it as 'preliminary studies' on fact storage.
confidence_note: Single retained paper, pre-LLM scale. The FFN-storage claim is later corroborated independently by ROME and MEMIT with different methods and models (see P01).

statement: Where the intervention sits decides what changes: ablating the ~50 FFN neurons that carry the refusal template changes response formatting on 80% of harmful prompts yet produces near-zero harmful compliance (the model still will not help), while ablating the single residual-stream refusal direction removes refusal of harmful instructions outright.
perturbation_kind: neuron ablation vs direction ablation (two-site contrast on one behavior family)
observed_effect: Liu et al.: 'The neurons control which refusal template the model uses, not whether it refuses' — ablation (0.014% of 350,208 FFN neurons, circuit width about 37, layers 29-35) moves 57% of 520 AdvBench prompts REFUSE to ENGAGE (a pre-training harm warning), 18% to UNCLEAR, with 3/520 harmful compliance, all with disclaimers. The same paper calls its behavioral direction d_F 'the unembedding-space analog of the residual-stream refusal direction identified by Arditi et al.' and localizes that direction's FFN sources. Safety is layered: the 50-neuron RLHF template (Regime 1) sits over a pre-training harm warning that survives 500-neuron ablation (Regime 2) over an indestructible factual layer (Regime 3). Arditi et al.: erasing the residual-stream refusal direction 'prevents it from refusing harmful instructions'.
scope: FFN template neurons (Qwen3-4B primary; 13 models across 4 architecture families in the sweep) vs residual-stream direction (13 open chat models up to 72B); safety refusal.
confidence_note: Full-text verified (arXiv PDF, 29 pp). Two papers, two sites, one behavior family: 'refusal' decomposes into a format component (FFN template) and a decision component (residual-stream direction), and the blast radius differs by site. The full text's random controls match the skill's DME-2c design: 50 random same-layer neurons changed the gap +0.2%, 50 early-layer neurons -0.7%. The verify step should measure both dimensions, not assume one 'refusal' metric.

statement: Directional steering has measured validity conditions: residual-stream direction injection switched English-to-Chinese output on 99.1% of prompts only in the 3 of 19 tested models satisfying three observed conditions (bilingual training, FFN-to-skip signal ratio between 0.3 and 1.1, linear representability), failed on the other 16 models and on math, code and factual circuits — defining the limits of directional steering; the FFN-to-skip ratio predicts the appropriate intervention.
observed_effect: 'residual-stream direction injection switches English to Chinese output on 99.1 percent of 580 benchmark prompts in the 3 of 19 tested models that satisfy three observed conditions ... The same intervention fails on the other 16 models and on math, code, and factual circuits, defining the limits of directional steering.'
scope: Routing-type circuits (pre-training behaviors distributed through attention); 13 models across 4 architecture families.
confidence_note: Single paper (2026): broad internal sweep (13 models), but no independent replication yet, and the FFN-to-skip ratio as predictor is the paper's own proposal. This entry bounds how far P04's low-rank steering generalizes.

statement: Small FFN-neuron sets causally shape aligned behaviors: ablating 20 neurons eliminated multi-turn sycophantic capitulation (36.7% to 0% on 30 questions), and 2x amplification of the same ~10-neuron circuit improved factual self-correction from 52% to 88% on 200 TruthfulQA prompts — but ablation and amplification trade off, because the same circuit carries both behaviors with opposite signs.
observed_effect: Liu et al. (Qwen3.5-2B): 20-neuron ablation eliminated capitulation on 0/30 questions (95% CI upper bound 10%); 2x amplification of 10 neurons raised correction 52% to 88% on 200 TruthfulQA prompts. The same circuit produces correction when the falsehood is in the prompt and capitulation when it follows the model's own answer — so ablating the 10 neurons also eliminated single-turn correction (51.5% to 0.0% on TruthfulQA). The dose-response is staircase-shaped, not smooth: two neurons each flip about 5 prompts (cooperative, not hierarchical), and the amplification window is narrow — 5x degraded coherence.
scope: Qwen3.5-2B (24 layers, ~147K FFN neurons); RLHF-organized behaviors (opposition circuits). On Qwen3-4B the sycophancy circuit is more distributed: 60% to 16.7% at N=50, never the blunt firm-maintenance responses seen at 2B.
confidence_note: Full-text verified (arXiv PDF, 29 pp). Same-circuit opposite-sign trade-off is quantified in the full text — 'amplification, rather than ablation, is the beneficial intervention for correction' — so 'local' holds across circuits, not within this circuit's own two behaviors. The staircase dose-response is a direct precedent for the skill's strength-series gate (DME-2d): expect graded but non-smooth behavior change.

statement: Patching design choices change what localization concludes: evaluation-metric and corruption-method choices produce 'disparate interpretability results' across localization and circuit-discovery settings, and the literature has no consensus hyperparameters.
observed_effect: 'varying these hyperparameters could lead to disparate interpretability results' in several settings of localization and circuit discovery; the paper issues recommendations on metrics and corruption methods going forward.
scope: Language-model localization and circuit discovery; directly relevant to the Localize step — corroborate a candidate site across patching variants (metric, corruption) before committing an edit to it. Methodological entry — propagation not applicable.
confidence_note: Methodological entry: propagation n/a. Single retained paper (ICLR 2024); the companion practitioner guide (Heimersheim & Nanda, arXiv:2404.15255) surfaced in the sweep but is not retained under the cap.

statement: Massive one-shot weight perturbations can be behavior-preserving when the perturbation is computed rather than blind: GPT-family models can be pruned to 50-60% sparsity in one shot without retraining at minimal accuracy loss — more than 100 billion weights ignorable at inference in OPT-175B/BLOOM-176B — and the method composes with weight quantization.
observed_effect: 'large-scale generative pretrained transformer (GPT) family models can be pruned to at least 50% sparsity in one-shot, without any retraining, at minimal loss of accuracy'; '60% unstructured sparsity with negligible increase in perplexity'; 'generalizes to semi-structured (2:4 and 4:8) patterns, and is compatible with weight quantization approaches'.
scope: OPT-175B, BLOOM-176B and smaller GPT-family models; second-order-compensated pruning (SparseGPT), not naive magnitude deletion.
confidence_note: Single retained paper (ICML 2023, heavily cited per search metadata). The contrast that matters here: a globally distributed weight perturbation can leave behavior nearly intact when each weight's update is computed against the others, while a sparse targeted perturbation can transform one behavior — the sparsity of the surface is not what determines the effect.

statement: The knowledge-editing field states its contract explicitly — to 'efficiently alter the behavior of LLMs within a specific domain without negatively impacting performance across other inputs' — and an exhaustive empirical comparison across method families finds enduring issues intrinsic to existing techniques.
perturbation_kind: survey-level: locate-then-edit, memory-based, meta-learning and other editing families
observed_effect: The survey provides 'an exhaustive overview of the task definition and challenges associated with model editing', 'an in-depth empirical analysis of the most progressive methods currently at our disposal', a new benchmark, and 'pinpoint[s] enduring issues intrinsic to existing techniques'.
scope: Editing method families as of EMNLP 2023 (incl. ROME-, MEND-, KN-, MEMIT-class methods); the contract quote is the same one anchoring the llm_editing ontology concept (operator ruling 2026-11-07). Methodological entry — propagation not applicable.
confidence_note: Methodological entry: propagation n/a. Use as the ground/route framing: an edit task is well-formed only when both halves of the contract — targeted change and preservation elsewhere — are measurable before the edit is planned.

statement: Steering interventions are not circuit-isolated: language-direction injection at therapeutic strength increased the safety refusal gap, but at higher strength the same injection dropped the safety gap by approximately 50% as the perturbation propagated through downstream layers where the safety circuit operates.
observed_effect: Liu et al.: 'at the therapeutic injection strength ..., language injection increases the safety refusal gap ..., but at higher strength ... the safety gap drops by approximately 50%, as the injection propagates through downstream layers where the safety circuit operates'; their own framing: 'Behavioral circuits are weakly coupled through layer dynamics, not independent modules.' The language injection has a sharp phase transition at alpha about 30 with a wide therapeutic window (40-100), and a mid-layer causal window (L9-22 on Qwen3-4B).
scope: Qwen3-4B, language (EN-to-ZH) direction injection interacting with the safety circuit; residual-stream interventions at mid layers.
confidence_note: Full-text verified. Single paper, but this is the authors' own measured limitation (no. 5 of their limitations list), not an abstract-level claim — a direct caution for the preservation gate: a direction validated on one circuit can degrade a different circuit at higher strength, so the preservation baseline must include the other circuit, and the strength series should bracket the intended operating point.

statement: A behavior's causal site need not be where training changed weights: the FFN neurons that causally carry RLHF-installed refusal had zero overlap with the parameters RLHF detectably modified — every detectable RLHF weight change above the salience floor was in attention projections (q/k/v/o_proj), and the causal FFN neurons appear to be pre-existing infrastructure that RLHF's attention changes route signals through.
perturbation_kind: fine-tune delta analyzed by module (base vs instruct weight diff)
observed_effect: Liu et al., comparing Qwen2.5-7B base with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct: '100% of RLHF modifications above this threshold were in the attention projections (q/k/v/o_proj). The neurons identified by our method had 0/50 overlap with weight-changed parameters at this threshold.' Their reading: 'The method identifies routing endpoints, not weight changes.'
scope: Qwen2.5-7B base vs Instruct, safety refusal; salience-floor-thresholded weight comparison (the base model already shows weak safety, gap about +4, that RLHF concentrates to about +16).
confidence_note: Full-text verified. Single paper; the salience floor is the authors' threshold, so 'no detectable change' is threshold-relative. For the localize step: contrast (failing vs progressing) can find a load-bearing site that training never wrote. The reverse implication matters for commissioning provenance: a site's causal role does not establish it as the site where the behavior was originally installed.

statement: The FFN substrate that locate-then-edit methods write into is an associative memory: transformer feed-forward layers operate as key-value memories whose keys correlate with training-text patterns and whose values induce output-vocabulary distributions — lower layers capture shallow patterns, upper layers semantic ones, with each layer's output a composition of its memories refined through the residual stream.
observed_effect: 'feed-forward layers in transformer-based language models operate as key-value memories, where each key correlates with textual patterns in the training examples, and each value induces a distribution over the output vocabulary'.
scope: Transformer language models (GPT-2-class upward); theory/analysis paper with no intervention. Grounds why mid-layer FFN sites are the storage substrate that ROME/MEMIT-class edits write to (see P01, O01, O02); FFN layers hold roughly two-thirds of a transformer's parameters. Substrate-theory entry — propagation not applicable.
confidence_note: Single retained paper (EMNLP 2021), but the FFN-storage claim it grounds is independently corroborated by the locate-then-edit line (ROME, MEMIT, knowledge neurons — P01/O01/O02) with different methods and models.

statement: Edits that pass their direct probe can be representationally shallow: under a belief-depth framework (generality, robustness, internal representations), mechanistic editing fails to implant knowledge deeply while synthetic-document finetuning often succeeds — the domain's most important negative result for the verify stage.
perturbation_kind: null-space batch edits (AlphaEdit) vs synthetic-document finetuning, evaluated for belief depth
observed_effect: 'simple prompting and mechanistic editing techniques fail to implant knowledge deeply' — mechanistic editing sits near baseline on generality (causal-implication implanted-belief rates of 0.06 for subtle and 0.12 for BKC facts, vs SDF's 0.80 and 0.83) and collapses under scrutiny, while SDF-implanted beliefs generalize to related contexts, withstand self-scrutiny and multi-turn adversarial debate, and are representationally similar to genuine knowledge (adversarial probes cannot distinguish the most plausible SDF facts).
scope: Scope conditions from the full text (90 pp, run ac3ac4bc3af5f4db): editor = AlphaEdit (a MEMIT-lineage null-space editor); primary models = Llama 3.3 70B Instruct and Llama 3.1 8B; facts were multi-clause narrative universe-contexts decomposed into single-sentence claims — harder than the single-fact regime AlphaEdit was designed for, and verbose context contaminates the subject key representation; scaling distinct rewrites per claim (2/20/100) did not improve mechanistic editing; rank-1 LoRA finetuning with sufficient epochs CAN implant deep beliefs — the shallowness is specific to algebraic locate-then-edit, not to low-rank weight updates as such. Evaluation entry — propagation not applicable (the finding is a failure of integration, not a blast radius).
confidence_note: Single paper (abstract extracted in run 4c02bf49b492711e; full text verified in run ac3ac4bc3af5f4db). Corroborating direction in Sharkey et al.'s catalog (full text, run ac3ac4bc3af5f4db): existing finetuning methodologies 'primarily make shallow edits to existing model representations and circuitry', and ROME-class localization 'has not yet found appropriate model components to intervene on' (citing Thibodeau 2022; Hase et al. 2023). For the skill: shallow is sufficient if the target is itself a surface blocker, not a missing capability — but the verify stage must test depth, not just the direct probe.
